```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "../../../AmberMakie/docs"))
using Amber, AmberMakie, CairoMakie
CairoMakie.activate!()
set_theme!(theme_amber_light())
```

A CMOS inverter is small enough to understand device by device, but rich
enough to demonstrate the two analyses at the heart of digital-cell
characterization. A DC sweep reveals logic levels and switching threshold;
a transient run reveals delay under a specified load.

## Model the complementary pair

The level-1 models include channel-length modulation, body effect, and gate
capacitances. The PMOS is deliberately half as strong as the NMOS, so the
transfer curve need not be perfectly symmetric.

```{julia}
const PROJECT_CMOS_NMOS = Level1MOSFET(threshold_voltage=0.7V,
    transconductance=2mA/V^2, channel_length_modulation=0.03/V,
    body_effect=0.35sqrt(V), surface_potential=0.35V,
    gate_source_capacitance=8pF, gate_drain_capacitance=2pF)
const PROJECT_CMOS_PMOS = Level1MOSFET(threshold_voltage=0.7V,
    transconductance=1mA/V^2, channel_length_modulation=0.03/V,
    body_effect=0.35sqrt(V), surface_potential=0.35V,
    gate_source_capacitance=8pF, gate_drain_capacitance=2pF)

@circuit ProjectCMOSInverter(; supply_voltage=5V, input_voltage=0V,
        waveform=nothing, load_capacitance=20pF) begin
    gnd = ground(); supply = node(); input = node(); output = node()
    VDD = voltage_source(supply, gnd; dc=supply_voltage)
    Input = voltage_source(input, gnd; dc=input_voltage, ac=1V, waveform)
    PullUp = pmos(output, input, supply, supply; model=PROJECT_CMOS_PMOS)
    PullDown = nmos(output, input, gnd, gnd; model=PROJECT_CMOS_NMOS)
    Load = capacitor(output, gnd; value=load_capacitance)
    observe(voltage(input), voltage(output), current(PullUp), current(PullDown),
        power(PullUp), power(PullDown))
end

check(ProjectCMOSInverter())
```

## Extract the DC voltage-transfer characteristic

Each point is a full nonlinear operating-point solution. Keeping the loop as
ordinary Julia makes the experiment transparent and lets us derive any metric
we want from the resulting arrays.

```{julia}
input_sweep = collect(range(0V, 5V; length=101))
output_sweep = [only(voltage(
    operating_point(ProjectCMOSInverter(input_voltage=value)), :output))
    for value in input_sweep]

switching_index = argmin(abs.(output_sweep .- input_sweep))
switching_voltage = input_sweep[switching_index]
low_output = last(output_sweep)
high_output = first(output_sweep)

(switching_voltage, low_output, high_output)
```

```{julia}
transfer_figure = Figure(size=(760, 610))
axis = Axis(transfer_figure[1, 1];
    xlabel="Input voltage (V)", ylabel="Output voltage (V)",
    title="DC voltage-transfer characteristic", aspect=1)
lines!(axis, input_sweep, output_sweep; color="#0072B2", linewidth=3)
lines!(axis, input_sweep, input_sweep; color=(:gray40, 0.65), linestyle=:dash)
scatter!(axis, [switching_voltage], [output_sweep[switching_index]];
    color="#D55E00", markersize=14)
transfer_figure
```

The dashed line is $V_{out}=V_{in}$. Its intersection with the transfer curve
is the inverter's static switching point for these device strengths.

## Drive a capacitive load

Now the same cell receives a 10 MHz pulse input with 1 ns edges. Exact event
handling prevents the integrator from stepping across an edge, while the
transistor capacitances and explicit 20 pF load determine the output dynamics.

```{julia}
switching_circuit = ProjectCMOSInverter(
    waveform=Pulse(low=0V, high=5V, frequency=10MHz,
        duty_cycle=0.5, rise=1ns, fall=1ns))
waveforms = transient(switching_circuit, 0s => 500ns;
    event_mode=:exact, max_step=1ns, saveat=0.5ns)

delay = propagation_delay(waveforms;
    input=voltage(:input), output=voltage(:output))

(propagation_delay=delay, load_capacitance=20pF)
```

```{julia}
switching_figure = Figure(size=(1000, 560))
traceplot(switching_figure[1, 1], waveforms; signals=[:input, :output],
    interval=250ns => 500ns)
Label(switching_figure[0, 1], "Loaded CMOS inverter at 10 MHz"; fontsize=21)
switching_figure
```

The opposite output transition is visible after every input edge. The reported
threshold-crossing delay measures the first transition. Unequal PMOS and NMOS
drive strengths also make the two edge shapes visibly different; changing their
transconductance ratio is the natural next design experiment.

::: {.callout-tip}
After sizing the pair for delay and switching point, use Amber's Monte Carlo
analysis to vary threshold voltage and transconductance, then reuse the
AmberMakie yield and correlation views from tutorial 11.
